simple.meaning: עֲלִיָּה (ʻălîyâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “something lofty , i.e. a stair-way ; also a second-story room (or even one on the roof); figuratively, the sky.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Judges 3:20. The surrounding context includes family line, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עֲלִיָּה (H5944) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: עֲלִיָּה (ʻălîyâh) / H5944 is traced through Judges 3:20, Judges 3:23, Judges 3:24, Judges 3:25 with generated occurrence evidence.

timeline.evidenceText: Ehud came to him; and he was sitting by himself alone in the cool upper room. Ehud said, “I have a message from God to you.” He arose out of his seat.
Then Ehud went out onto the porch, and shut the doors of the upper room on him, and locked them.
After he had gone, his servants came and saw that the doors of the upper room were locked. They said, “Surely he is covering his feet† or, “relieving himself”. in the upper room.”
They waited until they were ashamed; and behold, he didn’t open the doors of the upper room. Therefore they took the key and opened them, and behold, their lord had fallen down dead on the floor.
Joab was told, “Behold, the king weeps and mourns for Absalom.”
He said to her, “Give me your son.” He took him out of her bosom, and carried him up into the room where he stayed, and laid him on his own bed.
Elijah took the child, and brought him down out of the room into the house, and delivered him to his mother; and Elijah said, “Behold, your son lives.”

Ahaziah fell down through the lattice in his upper room that was in Samaria, and was sick. So he sent messengers, and said to them, “Go, inquire of Baal Zebub, the god of Ekron, whether I will recover of this sickness.”
Please let’s make a little room on the roof. Let’s set a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp stand for him there. When he comes to us, he can stay there.”
One day he came there, and he went to the room and lay there.

The king broke down the altars that were on the roof of the upper room of Ahaz, which the kings of Judah had made, and the altars which Manasseh had made in the two courts of Yahweh’s house, and beat them down from there, and cast their dust into the brook Kidron.
Then David gave to Solomon his son the plans for the porch of the temple, for its houses, for its treasuries, for its upper rooms, for its inner rooms, for the place of the mercy seat;

The weight of the nails was fifty shekels‡ A shekel is about 10 grams or about 0.32 Troy ounces, so 50 shekels was about 0.5 kilograms or about 16 Troy ounces. of gold. He overlaid the upper rooms with gold.

the food of his table, the seating of his servants, the attendance of his ministers, their clothing, his cup bearers also, their clothing, and his ascent by which he went up to Yahweh’s house; there was no more spirit in her.
After him, Malchijah, one of the goldsmiths to the house of the temple servants, and of the merchants, made repairs opposite the gate of Hammiphkad, and to the ascent of the corner.
Between the ascent of the corner and the sheep gate, the goldsmiths and the merchants made repairs.
He lays the beams of his rooms in the waters.
He waters the mountains from his rooms.
“Woe to him who builds his house by unrighteousness,
who says, ‘I will build myself a wide house and spacious rooms,’

definitions.short: something lofty , i.e. a stair-way ; also a second-story room (or even one on the roof); figuratively, the sky
definitions.usage: ascent, (upper) chamber, going up, loft, parlour.
definitions.full: H5944. aliyyah עֲלִיָּה noun feminine (c. adjective masculine Jer 22:14 , compare Albr ZAW xvi (1896), 83 Kö Synt. § 251 k ) roof-chamber (Late Hebrew id. , עֲלִיתָא ᵑ7 , Syriac (whence Arabic dining-room as loan-word Frä 20f. ); Sabean עלית DHM Epigr. Denkm. 27 ); — chamber on roof, cool and secluded: absolute ׳ע Judg 3:23-24 , 25 (compare Nes Marg. 13 ), 1Kin 17:19 , 23 ; 2Kin 4:11 ; construct הַמְּקֵרָה עֲלִיַּת Judg 3:20 , קִֿיר׳ע 2Kin 4:10 roof-chamber with walls (permanent); ׳ע הַשַּׁעַר 2Sam 19:1 , i.e. over the gateway; ׳ע הַמִּנָּה Neh 3:31-32 , i.e. at a corner of the wall; ׳ע אָחָז 2Kin 23:12 (probably built by A.); suffix עֲלִיָּתוֺ 1:2 (belonging to Ahaziah); — 2Chr 9:4 read עֹלֹתָיו (compare || 1Kin 10:5 ); plural absolute מְרֻוָּחִים עֲלִיּוֺת Jer 22:14 spacious roof-chambers ; in Solomon's temple according to 2Chr 3:9 , so suffix עֲלִיּתָיו 1Chr 28:11 ; more Generally עֲלִיּוֺתָיו Jer 22:13 ; ׳י 's chambers in sky Psa 104:3 , containing rain, 104:13 .
